module.purpose: Provides pointer-driven connection handling for a graph editor, including handle discovery, connection validation, auto-pan, connection lifecycle callbacks, and cleanup.
module.summary: This module coordinates the interactive lifecycle of creating or reconnecting graph edges from DOM handles. It translates pointer coordinates, waits for a configurable drag threshold, selects nearby handles, validates connection direction and connectability, updates in-progress connection state, optionally auto-pans the canvas, emits lifecycle callbacks, and removes listeners and animation frames when complete.
module.businessContext: Supports visual node-and-edge workflow editing. If it fails, users cannot reliably create or reconnect relationships between graph nodes.
functions: onPointerDown (~L25-238): Coordinates pointer-driven connection creation, validation, updates, callbacks, and cleanup.
autoPan (~L80-87): Repeatedly pans the canvas while the pointer approaches its boundary.
onPointerMove (~L124-191): Tracks pointer movement and updates the in-progress connection state.
onPointerUp (~L193-231): Completes or cancels connections and removes pointer listeners.
isValidHandle (~L241-310): Resolves a DOM handle and validates a candidate graph connection.

io: Registers and removes mousemove, mouseup, touchmove, and touchend listeners on the host document.
Queries DOM elements and the element under the pointer during handle validation.
mutationOfArg: Passes updated connection state to updateConnection and invokes supplied connection lifecycle callbacks.

preconditions: The event is a MouseEvent or TouchEvent.
The supplied DOM node, handle configuration, node lookup, and connection callbacks are compatible with the pointer-connection workflow.
postconditions: If the container bounds, handle type, or source handle cannot be resolved, the function exits without starting a connection.
When a gesture starts, the connection state is updated with an in-progress connection and onConnectStart is invoked when provided.
Pointer movement updates the in-progress connection with the current pointer position, candidate target handle, and validity.
On a completed valid connection, onConnect is invoked with the resulting connection when provided.

On pointer termination after a started gesture, onConnectEnd is invoked with the final connection state when provided, and onReconnectEnd is also invoked when edgeUpdaterType is set and the callback is provided.
The connection is cancelled and any scheduled auto-pan animation is cancelled when the pointer-up cleanup executes.
invariants: A connection is not started until drag distance exceeds dragThreshold, except when dragThreshold is zero.
The source handle remains the handle resolved at pointer-down for the duration of the gesture.
A touch pointer-up with one or more remaining touches does not abort or finalize the connection.
A connection is emitted only when a candidate handle or result DOM node exists, a connection result exists, and the result is valid.
Auto-pan is started at most once per gesture and repeatedly schedules itself through requestAnimationFrame while enabled.
edgeCases: If domNode has no bounds or edgeUpdaterType does not resolve to a handle type, the function returns without starting a connection.
If the source handle cannot be found in nodeLookup for the requested node, type, handle ID, and connection mode, the function returns without starting a connection.
Movement whose squared distance from the initial pointer position is less than or equal to dragThreshold squared does not start the connection.
A zero dragThreshold starts the connection immediately on pointer-down.
A pointer move after the source handle is no longer available invokes pointer-up handling instead of continuing the gesture.
A touch pointer-up while touches remain is ignored to prevent another touch from aborting the connection.
An invalid or absent target handle updates the in-progress state without emitting onConnect; the final target position is null when no target handle was selected.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Invalid or unresolved container, source-handle, or target-handle conditions are handled by early return, invalid connection state, or cancellation; no exception is specified.

detail.name: isValidHandle
detail.signature: function isValidHandle<NodeType extends NodeBase = NodeBase, EdgeType extends EdgeBase = EdgeBase>(event: MouseEvent | TouchEvent, { handle, connectionMode, fromNodeId, fromHandleId, fromType, doc, lib, flowId, isValidConnection = alwaysValid, nodeLookup }: IsValidParams<NodeType, EdgeType>)
preconditions: event is a MouseEvent or TouchEvent.
The parameter object supplies the document, library prefix, flow identifier, originating node information, and node lookup expected by IsValidParams.
postconditions: Returns a result object containing handleDomNode, isValid, connection, and toHandle.
If no candidate handle is available, the result has isValid false and connection null.
If a candidate handle lacks a node identifier or handle type, the result is returned invalid.
When a candidate handle has the required identity attributes, result.connection contains source, sourceHandle, target, and targetHandle oriented according to fromType.
invariants: The handle directly under the event position is preferred over the supplied or closest handle when it has the flow-handle CSS class.
The returned result is initialized with isValid false and toHandle null.
A target-originating operation reverses the source and target assignment relative to a source-originating operation.
edgeCases: When handle is absent, no handle DOM query is performed and the supplied-handle candidate is null.
When the event position is not over a flow handle and no supplied handle DOM node is found, the result remains invalid with connection null.
When the candidate element is missing data-nodeid or handle type, the result is returned invalid.
A candidate element is considered connectable only when it has both connectable and connectableend classes.
A handle under the event position takes precedence over another candidate even when the other candidate is closer by distance.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Returns a Result with isValid false; if no valid handle identity is available, connection remains null.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: An invalid Result object with handleDomNode set to the selected candidate, connection null when no connection can be formed, and toHandle null.

detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns an object shaped as { handleDomNode, isValid, connection, toHandle }. A constructed connection is shaped as { source, sourceHandle, target, targetHandle }.
